newsitem.title: UK: Telewest slashes jobs as losses widen.
newsitem.headline: Telewest slashes jobs as losses widen.

text.p: Telewest Communications Plc, Britain's second biggest cable television and telephone company, said on Thursday it would slash around 1,400 jobs -- about a quarter of its workforce -- as part of a business review.
Telewest simultaneously announced that pre-tax losses in the first half of the year had widended to 142.34 million pounds ($227.9 million) from 117.51 million.

But the company said it believed losses on a pre-tax level had peaked. Earnings before tax, depreciation, interest and amortisation (EBIDTA) rose to 16.37 million pounds from 7.07 million in the half year.
Telewest, whose network is around 70 percent built, said it would slow down the pace of the build programme and refocus its emphasis to sales and customer service.

In an effort to contain costs and maximise cashflow after five years of rapid expansion, Telewest said it was streamlining its seven regional franchise areas into four, simplifying its operating structure and focusing on the core products of cable TV, telephony and data services.
It expects the redundancy programme, which will cost around five million pounds, to lead to savings of about 40 million pounds in the first full year.

"We will focus on retention, adding incremental customers to our completed network, and increasing the number of services to which they subscribe," said chief executive Stephen Davidson in the results statement.

Davidson, who declined to comment further on how the group was evaluating an approach by its Nasdaq-listed, smaller rival NTL Inc, reiterated only that Telewest expected to be a player in the consolidating British cable market.

The company and its shares have been under pressure since the formation and flotation in April of Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC), the country's biggest cable group, after a four-way merger. Newspapers have reported that NTL is keen to merge with Telewest to form a 1.0 billion rival to CWC.

Telewest, whose network now passes 2.8 million homes and has a penetration rate of 34 percent, spent 232 million pounds of capital expenditure in the first six months of this year and expects to spend a similar amount in the second half.
But the group added that capital expenditure requirements would decline substantially as the network build programme slowed. Funding to complete the build is in place.

Telewest, which said it now had 559,963 cable television customers, 720,508 residential telephony customers and 82,601 business customers, has seen its shares fall from around 135p to 60p over the year.
The stock edged up 0.5p to 83p by 1330 GMT.
